name: shell
title: Shell
description: A sidebar that stays while the main region scrolls, and a drawer when it is narrow.
use: The frame of an application: a sidebar that stays in place, a main region, and optionally a header, an aside and a footer. By default the document scrolls; shell-fixed makes each region scroll by itself. Two columns that scroll away with the page and never collapse are written with utilities alone: flex and a width.

instead.when: The document scrolls as a whole and has no sidebar
A reader resizes the two panes with a handle

platform.fallback: Heights are measured in vh, so on a phone the foot of a column can sit under the browser's toolbars
The sidebar and the aside never leave the layout, and shell-toggle stays visible
The sidebar and the aside get no extra padding at their foot

classes.name: shell
classes.description: The frame: a grid at least as tall as the viewport and a size container named shell. It draws nothing

classes.name: shell-fixed
classes.description: The shell is exactly the viewport and each region scrolls by itself, for an inbox, an editor or a chat

classes.name: shell-header
classes.description: A header across the top of the shell; the sticky columns start --shell-header under it

classes.name: shell-sidebar
classes.description: The column at the start: sticky, as tall as the room left in the viewport, with its own scroll. It leaves the layout below 48rem of shell

classes.name: shell-main
classes.description: The main region: it takes the column that is left and never grows past it

classes.name: shell-aside
classes.description: A column at the end, sticky like the sidebar. It leaves the layout below 64rem of shell

classes.name: shell-footer
classes.description: A footer across the foot of the shell, under the columns and below the fold

classes.name: shell-toggle
classes.description: A control shown only while the sidebar is away, such as the button that opens the same navigation as a drawer

properties.name: --shell-header
properties.description: The room kept for a shell-header above the sticky columns; a navbar's height
